items.item: A repetition level is attached to every value in a repeated field's path, not just to the field that repeated — this topic's sku and note columns both carry repetition levels even though only item itself repeats.

at.step: Reveal: a repetition level per value, not per row

items.item: The maximum definition level for a leaf field equals the count of optional-or-repeated fields in its path, not the total path depth — sku (required, one repeated ancestor) tops out at 1, note (optional, one repeated ancestor) tops out at 2.

items.item: An empty list and a genuinely absent record are different facts that a flat column must be able to distinguish — this topic's own reassembly code would silently merge adjacent records without the definition-level-0 marker row.

at.step: Reveal: a NULL still needs a definition level

items.item: Reassembly needs only the current record's worth of repetition/definition levels in memory at a time, not the whole column, since a fresh repetition level of 0 is a self-contained signal to close the current record.

at.step: Reveal: reassembly walks both streams in lock-step

items.item: Arrow's offsets buffer is a running (cumulative) sum of item counts, while ORC's length stream stores each record's count directly — this topic's own code derives Arrow's per-record counts by subtracting consecutive offsets and asserts the result equals ORC's length stream exactly.

items.item: Arrow's list validity bitmap answers a different question than its offsets buffer: whether the list itself is null (not present at all) versus how many items it holds (which can legitimately be zero for a non-null, empty list).

at.step: Reveal: Arrow's answer — offsets, not levels

items.item: The per-record overhead measured in this topic's synthetic dataset (179 level entries for 159 actual items) comes entirely from records with empty lists, not from any per-value cost on records that do have items — the overhead is fixed per record, not proportional to nesting depth of the data itself.

at.deep: Lab: an empty list that still costs something

items.item: This topic's schema (one repeated field, one optional field inside it) is a shallower case of Dremel's own two-repeated-field worked example; the same level-counting rules apply at any depth, only the number of distinct values grows.

Dremel's own reassembly algorithm for deeper schemas needs a finite-state machine to pick the next field reader; this topic's single-repeated-field case needs no such machine because there is only one possible 'next reader' at any point.

All three formats in this topic are checked, not just described, to encode equivalent structural information for the same data: the worked example's Dremel reassembly, Arrow's derived item counts, and ORC's length stream are all asserted against each other or against the original records directly in examples.py.
